assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting artificial atom into a controllable, strongly coupled and readable quantum system in a microwave resonator, the architecture underlying dispersive readout, two-qubit gates and essentially all superconducting processors. It opened a genuinely new regime (strong coupling with one 'atom' on a chip), is clean and conceptually clear, and has become a platform for fundamental quantum optics as well as quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Huang, Schoelkopf and Wallraff define the 2004 proposal and first experiment; the supplied credit names Blais (theory), Wallraff and Schoelkopf (experiment), a coherent theory-plus-two-experiment configuration. Girvin and Devoret are intertwined with the origin and are not in the supplied credited names; the omission of Girvin is a real fairness question I cannot resolve from the list alone.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: reproduced and extended in dozens of laboratories, used daily in every superconducting quantum processor, and the interpretation is stable. The 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so there is a timing and balance question about a second circuits-centred prize so soon, and I have professional proximity to this field.
uncertainties: Whether a circuits prize so soon after 2025 is balanced, and whether the discovery should be framed as the physics of strong coupling rather than the quantum-computing application.
Credit allocation relative to Girvin, Devoret and Huang, who are not in the supplied names.
My own field and WACQT role may constitute a conflict of interest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the subsequent theory of analogue and digital quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions defined how controlled many-body quantum systems can be engineered. It is original, clear and has had decisive influence on experiments in ions, atoms and, by extension, other platforms.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the two obvious theory originators and form a natural pair; the supplied credit lists only them. Wineland (2012) and Haroche already received prizes for the experimental side, so this would recognize the proposal that guided it.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by ion-trap and neutral-atom experiments over thirty years; very mature, arguably overdue. A committee may hesitate over recognizing pure theory whose experimental realization was already honoured.
uncertainties: Whether the 2012 prize already covers much of the territory, making this a partial duplication.
Whether the prize would be for gates, for quantum simulation, or both, which affects scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record stability and accuracy, brought precision timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and enabled tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path toward redefinition of the second. The importance and concrete measurement achievement are very clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance frontier; credit is reasonably clean for two laureates. Hall and Hänsch (2005, frequency combs) and Wineland (2012) are earlier related prizes, and other groups (Lemonde, Gill, Hollberg, Ludlow) contributed, so a two-name pair omits some people.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced across many laboratories and confirmed in international comparisons; mature and timely as the redefinition of the second is discussed.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes on optical-frequency metrology.
Whether the pair adequately represents the contributions of strontium versus ytterbium and other clock efforts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the HgTe experiment and three-dimensional materials, created a new classification of band insulators and a very large field. The discovery is original and widely influential. Condensed-matter topology is outside my primary field, so I defer partly to colleagues on the relative weight.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical predictions; Molenkamp led the HgTe experimental confirmation (with Zhang and others on the proposal side). Hasan's ARPES work on three-dimensional materials is credited in the list, but selecting Kane, Mele and Molenkamp gives the cleanest configuration. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu are not in the supplied names, leaving a real attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in transport and photoemission over more than a decade; mature. The 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions, so topology has already been recognized in part.
uncertainties: Credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Molenkamp and Hasan is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states opened the moire materials field, a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The discovery is new, the field is very active and the impact is significant.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group did the decisive 2018 experiments, a clean theory-plus-experiment trio from the supplied names. Cao, Fatemi and others on the experimental side and Kim and Dean on related devices could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Strong reproducibility across many laboratories for the basic phenomena, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated states is still under active investigation, so it may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and phase diagram remain unsettled.
Whether the experimental credit should include Cao or other co-first authors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed vacuum injection, proposed by Caves and now routinely implemented in gravitational-wave detectors, beats the standard quantum limit in a macroscopic instrument. It is a clear case of a basic quantum-optics phenomenon becoming a working enabling tool, and I value the combination of a clean concept and demonstrated performance.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the 1981 proposal, and experimental development through Kimble, Slusher and others in the 1980s, with Schnabel and Mavalvala leading the gravitational-wave implementation. Kimble's early squeezing experiments are an important omission from the chosen trio, though he is in the credited names. Distribution of credit between the proposal, early squeezed-light generation and detector implementation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in GEO600, LIGO and Virgo, which now routinely run with squeezing; mature. The 2017 gravitational-wave prize may have absorbed some of the recognition.
uncertainties: Difficult attribution among proposers, early experimenters and detector implementers.
Possible perception that gravitational-wave recognition was already provided in 2017.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realizing the Bose-Hubbard and Fermi-Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, gave a clean and tunable quantum simulator. It opened a new regime of controllable many-body physics and has been reproduced widely.
assessment.attribution: Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger delivered the decisive experiments; Jaksch, Zoller and Cirac proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization and are in the credited names. A three-experimentalist prize would leave the theory proposal to be handled separately or overlapped with the Cirac and Zoller candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed; quantum-gas microscopes and fermionic realizations followed. The 2001 and 1997 prizes cover adjacent cold-atom work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller entry and with earlier cold-atom prizes.
Quantum simulators have not yet solved an open problem such as the Hubbard-model phase diagram.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought mechanical resonators to their quantum ground state and enabled quantum control of macroscopic motion, including strong coupling and squeezing. It is closely linked to the circuit and waveguide quantum-optics physics I know well. The question I would press is whether the work opened a distinct new regime of physics rather than extending known quantum-optical techniques.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer, Painter and Kippenberg are leading figures, but ground-state cooling and quantum control also owe much to Teufel, Lehnert, Cleland, O'Connell and Schwab, who are not in the supplied names. The attribution is therefore not clean.
assessment.maturity: Well reproduced, with the field mature, but the strongest results, such as macroscopic entanglement and quantum transduction, are still developing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Several decisive contributors are absent from the supplied credit.
Distinct physical novelty compared with earlier cooling and quantum-optics results is debatable.
Applications such as transduction remain unproven.
